source_quote: Therefore, Lebanon  is  working  towards    the establishment of the Lebanon Green Investment  Facility  (LGIF) as  stipulated  in  the Government's Financial Recovery Plan, to provide climate and green finance through accessible  and  affordable  finance  instruments for both the public and private sectors, as well as to provide needed technical assistance to various entities to create bankable projects. The LGIF  is  foreseen  to  substantially  contribute  to the  implementation  of  the  NDC  by  increasing investments to climate-friendly projects, through strong donor and investor coordination mechanism and capitalization strategy.
section_header: ## 6. Support Needed for NDC Implementation and Achievement
extraction_rationale: Named climate-finance facility with target users and NDC role.

policy_statement: Develop a climate-proofing methodology to assess climate-negative projects and guide investment evaluation.
source_quote: Moreover, Lebanon  is  currently  developing  a climate-proofing  methodology which  aims  to assess and reduce the impacts of climatenegative projects, as well as potentially guide the evaluation  of  investments,  through  a  climatelens.
section_header: ## 6. Support Needed for NDC Implementation and Achievement
extraction_rationale: Specific climate-screening methodology under development.

policy_statement: Explore greening foreign investments, including ODA, to accelerate the NDC and avoid carbon lock-in.
source_quote: Ultimately, Lebanon intends to explore the possibility of greening foreign investments including Official Development Assistance (ODA) to  accelerate the achievement of the NDC and avoid locking in  carbon  emissions  on  the  longterm.
section_header: ## 6. Support Needed for NDC Implementation and Achievement
extraction_rationale: Finance-screening policy direction; somewhat tentative because it says 'explore the possibility.'

policy_statement: Include Environmental and Social Standards and gender-responsiveness in project evaluation and implementation.
source_quote: Finally, the consideration of Environmental  and  Social  Standards  (ESS),  as well as gender-responsiveness should be included in projects' evaluation and implementation.
section_header: ## 6. Support Needed for NDC Implementation and Achievement
extraction_rationale: Project-evaluation requirement linked to NDC implementation; broader than climate alone.

policy_statement: Use the GCF country programme to clarify support needs and guide investors and donors on NDC priorities.
source_quote: Lebanon plans to make its support needs clear, starting  with  the  Green  Climate  Fund  (GCF)'s country programme for Lebanon. The programme plans to provide guidance for investors  and  donors  on  NDC  priorities,  which will be in line with the planned investments for economic recovery.
section_header: ## 6. Support Needed for NDC Implementation and Achievement
extraction_rationale: Named climate-finance planning programme.

policy_statement: Use NDC Partnership Plans to identify sectoral enabling activities and needs for NDC implementation, climate action, and transparency.
source_quote: Furthermore, the NDC Partnership Plans under development will deliver an overview of sectoral  enabling  activities  and  needs for  the implementation  of  the  NDC,  both  for  climate action and climate transparency.
section_header: ## 6. Support Needed for NDC Implementation and Achievement
extraction_rationale: Named planning instrument for NDC implementation needs.

policy_statement: California will reduce statewide greenhouse gas emissions to 1990 levels by 2020, equal to 427 MMTCO2E.
source_quote: In December 2007, ARB approved a greenhouse gas emissions target for 2020 equivalent to the state's calculated greenhouse gas emissions level in 1990. ARB developed the 2020 target after extensive technical work and a series of stakeholder meetings. The 2020 target of 427 MMTCO2E requires the reduction of 169 MMTCO2E, or approximately 30 percent, from the state's projected 2020 emissions of 596 MMTCO2E (business-as-usual) and the reduction of 42 MMTCO2E, or almost 10 percent, from 2002-2004 average emissions.
section_header: ## C. California's Greenhouse Gas Emissions and the 2020 Target
extraction_rationale: Quantified statewide GHG target with statutory context and 2020 deadline.

policy_statement: California will pursue an 80 percent GHG reduction below 1990 levels by 2050.
source_quote: Getting to the 2020 goal is not the end of the State's effort. According to climate scientists, California and the rest of the developed world will have to cut emissions by 80 percent from today's levels to stabilize the amount of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere and prevent the most severe effects of global climate change. This long range goal is reflected in California Executive Order S-3-05 that requires an 80 percent reduction of greenhouse gases from 1990 levels by 2050.
extraction_rationale: Long-term quantified mitigation target established by Executive Order.

policy_statement: California State government will reduce its own greenhouse gas emissions at least 30 percent below estimated business-as-usual emissions by 2020.
source_quote: While State government has already accomplished much to reduce its greenhouse gas emissions, it can and must do more. State agencies must lead by example by continuing to reduce their greenhouse gas emissions. Therefore, California State government has established a target of reducing its greenhouse gas emissions by a minimum of 30 percent below its estimated business-as-usual emissions by 2020 - approximately a 15 percent reduction from current levels.
section_header: ## A. The Role of State Government:  Setting an Example
extraction_rationale: Quantified operational emissions target for State government.

policy_statement: State agencies will bring climate change considerations into policies, planning, analysis, fleets, buildings, water, natural resources, and infrastructure management.
source_quote: California is committed to once again lead and support a pioneering effort to protect the environment and improve public health while maintaining a vibrant economy. Every agency, department and division will bring climate change considerations into its policies, planning and analysis, building and expanding current efforts to green its fleet and buildings, and managing its water, natural resources, and infrastructure to reduce greenhouse gas emissions.
extraction_rationale: Government-wide operational and planning commitment with specific emissions-reduction domains.

policy_statement: California will adopt amended CEQA Guidelines by January 1, 2010 to guide treatment of greenhouse gases in CEQA documents.
source_quote: The Governor's Office of Planning and Research and the Resources Agency are developing proposed amendments to the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines to provide guidance on how to address greenhouse gases in CEQA documents. As required by SB 97 (Chapter 185, Statutes of 2007), the amended CEQA guidelines will be adopted by January 1, 2010.
section_header: ## A. The Role of State Government:  Setting an Example
extraction_rationale: Binding climate-related planning and permitting guidance action with a statutory deadline.

policy_statement: ARB will support local government GHG inventories and reduction goals through protocols, tools, and guidance.
source_quote: To provide local governments guidance on how to inventory and report greenhouse gas emissions from government buildings, facilities, vehicles, wastewater and potable water treatment facilities, landfill and composting facilities, and other government operations, ARB recently adopted the Local Government Operations Protocol. ARB encourages local governments to use this protocol to track their progress in achieving reductions from municipal operations. ARB is also developing an additional protocol for community emissions.
section_header: ## B. The Role of Local Government: Essential Partners
extraction_rationale: Concrete local-government emissions accounting policy. It supports local climate targets, though local adoption is encouraged rather than mandated.

policy_statement: ARB encourages local governments to adopt municipal and community-wide GHG reduction goals paralleling the State target of approximately 15 percent below current levels by 2020.
source_quote: In addition to tracking emissions using these protocols, ARB encourages local governments to adopt a reduction goal for municipal operations emissions and move toward establishing similar goals for community emissions that parallel the State commitment to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by approximately 15 percent from current levels by 2020. To consolidate climate action resources and aid local governments in their emission reduction efforts, the ARB is developing various tools and guidance for use by local governments, including the next generation of best practices, case studies, a calculator to help calculate local greenhouse gas emissions, and other decision support tools.
section_header: ## B. The Role of Local Government: Essential Partners
extraction_rationale: Quantified recommended local-government emissions goal supported by ARB tools and guidance; not a binding mandate.

policy_statement: California will implement discrete early action GHG regulations and programs, all adopted and effective by January 1, 2010.
source_quote: In September 2007, ARB approved a list of nine Discrete Early Actions to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and is currently in the process of developing regulations and programs based on these measures. Regulations implementing the Discrete Early Action measures must be adopted and in effect by January 1, 2010 (HSC §38560.5 (b)). All the Discrete Early Actions are included in the recommended measures and are shown below in Table 4.
extraction_rationale: Umbrella initiative with a statutory adoption/effective date and a list of specific early-action measures.

parent_statement: Discrete Early Actions
policy_statement: ARB will implement nine discrete early actions, including ship electrification, high-GWP controls, aerodynamic efficiency, landfill gas capture, tire inflation, and the Low Carbon Fuel Standard.
source_quote: In September 2007, ARB approved a list of nine Discrete Early Actions to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and is currently in the process of developing regulations and programs based on these measures. Regulations implementing the Discrete Early Action measures must be adopted and in effect by January 1, 2010 (HSC §38560.5 (b)). All the Discrete Early Actions are included in the recommended measures and are shown below in Table 4.
extraction_rationale: Specific listed early-action measures with Board consideration/adoption dates. Several are also described later in detail; this extraction captures the early-action schedule.

policy_statement: California will implement a broad-based cap-and-trade program linked to Western Climate Initiative partners.
source_quote: Implement a broad-based California cap-and-trade program to provide a firm limit on emissions. Link the California cap-and-trade program with other Western Climate Initiative Partner programs to create a regional market system to achieve greater environmental and economic benefits for California. Ensure California's program meets all applicable AB 32 requirements for market-based mechanisms.
section_header: ## 1.  California Cap-and-Trade Program Linked to Western Climate Initiative Partner Jurisdictions
extraction_rationale: Named umbrella carbon-pricing program with multiple design sub-actions.

parent_statement: California Cap-and-Trade Program Linked to Western Climate Initiative Partner Jurisdictions
policy_statement: California will develop cap-and-trade regulations by January 1, 2011, and begin the program in 2012.
source_quote: Based on the requirements of AB 32, regulations to implement the cap-and-trade program need to be developed by January 1, 2011, with the program beginning in 2012. This rule development schedule will be coordinated with the WCI timeline for developing a regional cap-and-trade program.
section_header: ## 1.  California Cap-and-Trade Program Linked to Western Climate Initiative Partner Jurisdictions
extraction_rationale: Specific rulemaking deadline and program start date for cap-and-trade.

parent_statement: California Cap-and-Trade Program Linked to Western Climate Initiative Partner Jurisdictions
policy_statement: California's cap-and-trade program will cap about 85 percent of statewide GHG emissions.
source_quote: By providing a firm cap on 85 percent of the state's greenhouse gas emissions, the cap-and-trade regulatory program is an essential component of the overall plan to meet the 2020 target and provides a robust mechanism to achieve the additional reductions needed by 2050. To meet the emissions reduction target under AB 32, the limit on emissions allowed under the cap, plus emissions from uncapped sources, must be no greater than the 2020 emissions goal.
extraction_rationale: Quantified coverage parameter for the cap-and-trade program.

parent_statement: California Cap-and-Trade Program Linked to Western Climate Initiative Partner Jurisdictions
policy_statement: The cap-and-trade program will phase in covered sectors in 2012 and 2015, including electricity, large industrial sources, fuels, and transportation fuels.
source_quote: The proposed cap-and-trade measure phases in the following sectors: Starting in the first compliance period (2012): - Electricity generation, including imports not covered by a WCI Partner jurisdiction - Large industrial facilities that emit over 25,000 metric tons CO2E per year. Starting in the second compliance period (2015): - Upstream treatment of industrial fuel combustion at facilities with emissions at or below 25,000 metric tons CO2E, and all commercial and residential fuel combustion regulated where the fuel enters into commerce - Transportation fuel combustion regulated where the fuel enters into commerce.
extraction_rationale: Specific sector coverage, emissions threshold, and phase-in dates.

parent_statement: California Cap-and-Trade Program Linked to Western Climate Initiative Partner Jurisdictions
policy_statement: California will link allowance budgets and trading with WCI partner jurisdictions.
source_quote: To achieve the individual WCI Partner jurisdiction goals and the regional goal, each WCI Partner jurisdiction will have an allowance budget based on its goal that declines to 2020. For example, California's allowance budget will be based on the level of emissions needed to achieve the AB 32 target for 2020, as described above. Once California links with the other WCI Partner jurisdictions, allowances could be traded across state and provincial boundaries.
section_header: ## Linkage with the Western Climate Initiative Partner Jurisdictions
extraction_rationale: Concrete cross-jurisdictional carbon-market linkage mechanism.

parent_statement: California Cap-and-Trade Program Linked to Western Climate Initiative Partner Jurisdictions
policy_statement: The WCI-linked program will phase in allowance auctions, starting at 10 percent and increasing to 25 percent by 2020.
source_quote: In addition, the WCI Partner jurisdictions have agreed to phase in regionally coordinated auctions of allowances, with a minimum percentage of allowances auctioned in each period starting with 10 percent in the first compliance period and increasing to 25 percent in 2020. WCI partners aspire to reach higher auction percentages over time, possibly to 100 percent. Under the program design, each WCI Partner jurisdiction, including California, can auction a greater portion of its allowance budget in any compliance period.
section_header: ## Linkage with the Western Climate Initiative Partner Jurisdictions
extraction_rationale: Quantified auction schedule for emissions allowances.

parent_statement: California Cap-and-Trade Program Linked to Western Climate Initiative Partner Jurisdictions
policy_statement: ARB will evaluate allowance set-asides to reward early action, support efficiency and land-use measures, and target disadvantaged communities.
source_quote: Emission allowances represent a significant economic value whether they are freely allocated or sold through auction. Section E includes a preliminary discussion of some of the options that have been suggested for use of allowance value or revenues. ARB will evaluate the possible uses of allowances or revenues as part of the rulemaking process.
extraction_rationale: Specific potential use of allowances; still under rulemaking evaluation.

parent_statement: California Cap-and-Trade Program Linked to Western Climate Initiative Partner Jurisdictions
policy_statement: ARB will establish offset rules for cap-and-trade compliance and limit offset and other outside-system allowance use to no more than 49 percent of required reductions.
source_quote: The cap-andtrade rulemaking will establish appropriate rules for use of offsets. As required by AB 32, any reduction of greenhouse gas emissions used for compliance purposes must be real, permanent, quantifiable, verifiable, enforceable, and additional (HSC §38562(d)(1) and (2)). Offsets used to meet regulatory requirements must be quantified according to Board-adopted methodologies, and ARB must adopt a regulation to verify and enforce the reductions (HSC §38571).
extraction_rationale: Specific compliance-offset mechanism for the cap-and-trade financial instrument. The 49 percent limit is specified later in the same Offsets subsection.

policy_statement: California will implement Pavley light-duty vehicle GHG standards, develop a second phase, and align zero-emission vehicle and clean-fuel technology programs with climate goals.
source_quote: Implement adopted Pavley standards and planned second phase of the program. Align zero-emission vehicle, alternative and renewable fuel and vehicle technology programs with long-term climate change goals. Passenger vehicles are responsible for almost 30 percent of California's greenhouse gas emissions.
section_header: ## 2.  California Light-Duty Vehicle Greenhouse Gas Standards
extraction_rationale: Named umbrella policy for passenger vehicle GHG reduction with subprograms.

parent_statement: California Light-Duty Vehicle Greenhouse Gas Standards
policy_statement: ARB will implement Pavley I standards and adopt a more stringent Pavley II phase.
source_quote: AB 1493 (Pavley, Chapter 200, Statutes of 2002) directed ARB to adopt vehicle standards that lowered greenhouse gas emissions to the maximum extent technologically feasible, beginning with the 2009 model year. ARB adopted regulations in 2004 and applied to the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (U.S. EPA) for a waiver under the federal Clean Air Act to implement the regulation. To obtain additional reductions from the light duty fleet, ARB plans to adopt a second, more stringent, phase of the Pavley regulations.
extraction_rationale: Binding vehicle-emission standard with a planned second phase.

parent_statement: California Light-Duty Vehicle Greenhouse Gas Standards
policy_statement: ARB will evaluate a feebate program as a Pavley backstop or supplement to achieve equivalent or greater GHG reductions.
source_quote: ARB is evaluating the use of feebates as a measure to achieve additional reductions from the mobile source sector, either as a backstop to the Pavley regulation if the regulation cannot be implemented, or as a supplement to Pavley if the waiver is approved and the regulation takes effect. AB 32 specifically states that if the Pavley regulations do not remain in effect, ARB shall implement alternative regulations to control mobile sources to achieve equivalent or greater reductions of greenhouse gas emissions (HSC §38590). ARB is currently evaluating the use of a feebate program as the mechanism to secure these reductions.
extraction_rationale: Specific fee/rebate financial mechanism under evaluation.

parent_statement: California Light-Duty Vehicle Greenhouse Gas Standards
policy_statement: California will continue and optimize the Zero Emission Vehicle program to require increasing numbers of zero- and near-zero-emission vehicles.
source_quote: The Zero Emission Vehicle (ZEV) program will play an important role in helping California meet its 2020 and 2050 greenhouse gas emissions reduction requirements. Through 2012, the program requires placement of hundreds of ZEVs (including hydrogen fuel cell and battery electric vehicles) and thousands of near-zero emission vehicles (plug-in hybrids, conventional hybrids, compressed natural gas vehicles). In the mid-term (2012-2015), the program will require placement of increasing numbers of ZEVs and near-zero emission vehicles in California.
extraction_rationale: Regulatory vehicle-technology program with deployment requirements.

parent_statement: California Light-Duty Vehicle Greenhouse Gas Standards
policy_statement: California will fund clean vehicle, alternative fuel, and advanced vehicle technology deployment through AB 118 programs.
source_quote: Under AB 118 (Núñez, Chapter 750, Statutes of 2007), ARB is administering the Air Quality Improvement Program, which provides approximately $50 million per year for grants to fund clean vehicle/equipment projects and research on the air quality impacts of alternative fuels and advanced technology vehicles. AB 118 also created the Alternative and Renewable Fuel and Vehicle Technology Program and authorized CEC to spend up to $120 million per year for over seven years (from 2008-2015) to develop, demonstrate, and deploy innovative technologies to transform California's fuel and vehicle types.
section_header: ## Air Quality Improvement Program/Alternative and Renewable Fuel and Vehicle Technology Program
extraction_rationale: Specific public funding and grant program for clean vehicle and fuel technologies.

policy_statement: California will maximize building and appliance energy efficiency standards and expand energy-efficiency investment and programs.
source_quote: Maximize energy efficiency building and appliance standards, and pursue additional efficiency efforts including new technologies, and new policy and implementation mechanisms. Pursue comparable investment in energy efficiency from all retail providers of electricity in California (including both investor-owned and publiclyowned utilities). Energy-efficiency measures for both electricity and natural gas can reduce greenhouse gas emissions significantly.
extraction_rationale: Umbrella resource-efficiency policy with multiple sub-strategies and quantified targets.

parent_statement: Energy Efficiency
policy_statement: California will target annual energy demand reductions of 32,000 GWh and 800 million therms from business as usual.
source_quote: This measure would set new targets for statewide annual energy demand reductions of 32,000 gigawatt hours and 800 million therms from business as usual - enough to power more than 5 million homes, or replace the need to build about ten new large power plants (500 megawatts each). These targets represent a higher goal than existing efficiency targets established by CPUC for the investor-owned utilities due to the inclusion of innovative strategies above traditional utility programs. Achieving the State's energy efficiency targets will require coordinated efforts from the State, the federal government, energy companies and customers.
extraction_rationale: Quantified energy-efficiency target with stated implementation collaboration.

parent_statement: Energy Efficiency
policy_statement: California will pursue zero-net-energy buildings, strengthened codes and standards, whole-building retrofits, local programs, water efficiency, and real-time energy information.
source_quote: Key energy efficiency strategies, grouped by type, include: Cross-cutting Strategy for Buildings - 'Zero Net Energy' buildings. Codes and Standards Strategies - Broader standards for new types of appliances and for water efficiency - More stringent building codes and appliance efficiency standards - Improved compliance and enforcement of existing standards - Voluntary efficiency and green building targets beyond mandatory codes.
extraction_rationale: Grouped list of named energy-efficiency interventions supporting the quantified target.

parent_statement: Energy Efficiency
policy_statement: California will implement a ten-year, $250 million solar water-heater incentive program to install 200,000 systems by 2017.
source_quote: Solar water heating systems offer a potential for natural gas savings in California. A solar water heating system offsets the use of natural gas by using the sun to heat water, typically reducing the need for conventional water heating by about two-thirds. The Solar Hot Water and Efficiency Act of 2007 (SHWEA) authorized a ten year, $250-million incentive program for solar water heaters with a goal of promoting the installation of 200,000 systems in California by 2017.
extraction_rationale: Funded incentive program with budget, deployment target, and deadline.

parent_statement: Energy Efficiency
policy_statement: California will target an additional 4,000 MW of combined heat and power capacity by 2020.
source_quote: Combined heat and power (CHP), also referred to as cogeneration, produces electricity and useful thermal energy in an integrated system. The widespread development of efficient CHP systems would help displace the need to develop new, or expand existing, power plants. This measure sets a target of an additional 4,000 MW of installed CHP capacity by 2020, enough to displace approximately 30,000 GWh of demand from other power generation sources.
extraction_rationale: Quantified CHP deployment target by 2020.

policy_statement: California will achieve a statewide renewable electricity mix of 33 percent by 2020.
source_quote: Achieve 33 percent renewable energy mix statewide. CEC estimates that about 12 percent of California's retail electric load is currently met with renewable resources. Based on Governor Schwarzenegger's call for a statewide 33 percent RPS, the Plan anticipates that California will have 33 percent of its electricity provided by renewable resources by 2020, and includes the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions based on this level.
extraction_rationale: Quantified renewable electricity target with 2020 deadline.

policy_statement: California will consider a feed-in tariff for RPS-eligible renewable energy facilities up to 20 MW.
source_quote: Another key action that may help to achieve the renewable energy goals is to reduce the complexity and cost faced by small renewable developers in contracting with utilities to supply renewable generation. This is particularly important for projects offering below 20 megawatts of generation capacity. One such option may be a feedin tariff for all RPS-eligible renewable energy facilities up to 20 megawatts in size.
extraction_rationale: Specific financial/rate mechanism, framed as a possible option.

policy_statement: ARB will develop and adopt a Low Carbon Fuel Standard reducing transportation-fuel carbon intensity by at least 10 percent by 2020.
source_quote: Develop and adopt the Low Carbon Fuel Standard. Because transportation is the largest single source of greenhouse gas emissions in California, the State is taking an integrated approach to reducing emissions from this sector. To reduce the carbon intensity of transportation fuels, ARB is developing a Low Carbon Fuel Standard (LCFS), which would reduce the carbon intensity of California's transportation fuels by at least ten percent by 2020 as called for by Governor Schwarzenegger in Executive Order S-01-07.
extraction_rationale: Named regulatory fuel standard with quantified carbon-intensity target and deadline.

policy_statement: ARB will develop regional passenger-vehicle GHG reduction targets for 2020 and 2035 through SB 375.
source_quote: Develop regional greenhouse gas emissions reduction targets for passenger vehicles. On September 30, 2008, Governor Arnold Schwarzenegger signed Senate Bill 375 (Steinberg) which establishes mechanisms for the development of regional targets for reducing passenger vehicle greenhouse gas emissions. SB 375 requires ARB to develop, in consultation with metropolitan planning organizations (MPOs), passenger vehicle greenhouse gas emissions reduction targets for 2020 and 2035 by September 30, 2010.
extraction_rationale: Statutory target-setting process with target years and deadline.

policy_statement: Metropolitan planning organizations must prepare sustainable communities strategies to reach ARB regional GHG targets.
source_quote: SB 375 requires MPOs to prepare a sustainable communities strategy to reach the regional target provided by ARB. MPOs would use the sustainable communities strategy for the land use pattern underlying the region's transportation plan. If the strategy does not meet the target, the MPO must document the impediments and show how the target could be met with an alternative planning strategy.
extraction_rationale: Binding land-use and transportation planning requirement linked to GHG targets.

policy_statement: Regional and local agencies should consider congestion pricing, indirect source rules, transit incentives, telework, car sharing, parking policies, public education, and related trip-reduction measures.
source_quote: Supporting measures that should be considered in both the regional target-setting and sustainable communities strategy processes include the following: Congestion pricing strategies can provide a method of efficiently managing traffic demand while raising funds for needed transit, biking and pedestrian infrastructure investment. Programs to reduce vehicle trips while preserving personal mobility, such as employee transit incentives, telework programs, car sharing, parking policies, public education programs and other strategies that enhance and complement land use and transit strategies can be implemented and coordinated by regional and local agencies and stakeholder groups.
extraction_rationale: Specific transportation demand-management interventions; some are recommendations and authority-limited.

policy_statement: California will permit voluntary pay-as-you-drive insurance to financially reward driving less.
source_quote: Another way to encourage greenhouse gas reductions from vehicle travel is through pay as you drive insurance (PAYD), a structure in which drivers realize a direct financial benefit from driving less. The California Insurance Commissioner recently announced support for PAYD and has proposed regulations to permit PAYD on a voluntary basis.
extraction_rationale: Specific proposed regulatory/financial mechanism to reduce vehicle travel.

policy_statement: California will implement light-duty vehicle efficiency measures, including tire inflation, efficient tires, lower-friction oil, and reduced air-conditioning load.
source_quote: Implement light-duty vehicle efficiency measures. Several additional measures could reduce light-duty vehicle greenhouse gas emissions. ARB is pursuing a regulation to ensure that tires are properly inflated when vehicles are serviced.
extraction_rationale: Named vehicle-efficiency measure with specific interventions and GHG purpose.

parent_statement: Vehicle Efficiency Measures
policy_statement: ARB will adopt a tire-inflation regulation, and CEC will develop an efficient tire program with potential minimum standards and consumer information requirements.
source_quote: In addition, CEC in consultation with CIWMB is developing an efficient tire program focusing first on data gathering and outreach, then on potential adoption of minimum fuel-efficient tire standards, and lastly on the development of consumer information requirements for replacing tires. ARB is also pursuing ways to reduce engine load via lower friction oil and reducing the need for air conditioner use. ARB is actively engaged in the regulatory development process for the tire inflation component of this measure.
extraction_rationale: Specific vehicle efficiency regulations/programs supporting the parent measure.

policy_statement: California will implement shore-power regulations for ships at berth and improve efficiency in goods movement.
source_quote: Implement adopted regulations for the use of shore power for ships at berth. Improve efficiency in goods movement activities. A significant portion of greenhouse gas emissions from transportation activities comes from the movement of freight or goods throughout the state.
extraction_rationale: Umbrella freight-sector efficiency policy with submeasures.

parent_statement: Goods Movement
policy_statement: ARB will implement adopted ship electrification regulations at ports.
source_quote: Both the Goods Movement Emission Reduction Plan (GMERP) and the 2007 State Implementation Plan (SIP) contain numerous measures designed to reduce the public health impact of goods movement activities in California. ARB has already adopted a regulation to require ship electrification at ports. Proposition 1B funds, as well as clean air plans being implemented by California's ports, will also help reduce greenhouse gas emissions while cutting criteria pollutant and toxic diesel emissions.
extraction_rationale: Specific adopted regulation requiring port electrification.

parent_statement: Goods Movement
policy_statement: ARB will develop and implement additional measures to reduce GHG emissions from trucks, ports, and related goods-movement facilities.
source_quote: ARB is proposing to develop and implement additional measures to reduce greenhouse gas emissions due to goods movement from trucks, ports and other related facilities. The anticipated reductions would be above and beyond what is already expected in the GMERP and the SIP. This effort should provide accompanying reductions in air toxics and smog forming emissions.
extraction_rationale: Concrete commitment to develop additional goods-movement GHG measures.

policy_statement: California will install 3,000 MW of solar-electric capacity under existing solar programs by 2017.
source_quote: Install 3,000 MW of solar-electric capacity under California's existing solar programs. As part of Governor Schwarzenegger's Million Solar Roofs Program, California has set a goal to install 3,000 megawatts (MW) of new solar capacity by 2017 - moving the state toward a cleaner energy future and helping lower the cost of solar systems for consumers. The Million Solar Roofs Initiative is a ratepayer-financed incentive program aimed at transforming the market for rooftop solar systems by driving down costs over time.
extraction_rationale: Named incentive program with quantified deployment target and deadline.

policy_statement: California will adopt medium- and heavy-duty vehicle efficiency measures.
source_quote: Adopt medium and heavy-duty vehicle efficiency measures. Medium- and heavy-duty vehicles account for approximately 20 percent of the transportation greenhouse gas inventory. Requiring retrofits to improve the fuel efficiency of heavy-duty trucks could include a requirement for devices that reduce aerodynamic drag and rolling resistance.
extraction_rationale: Umbrella vehicle efficiency policy with aerodynamic and hybridization submeasures.

parent_statement: Medium/Heavy-Duty Vehicles
policy_statement: California will pursue heavy-duty aerodynamic efficiency retrofits and medium/heavy-duty vehicle hybridization.
source_quote: Medium- and heavy-duty vehicles account for approximately 20 percent of the transportation greenhouse gas inventory. Requiring retrofits to improve the fuel efficiency of heavy-duty trucks could include a requirement for devices that reduce aerodynamic drag and rolling resistance. In addition, hybridization of medium- and heavy-duty vehicles would also reduce greenhouse gas emissions through increased fuel efficiency.
extraction_rationale: Specific vehicle technologies listed under the parent measure.

policy_statement: California will reduce industrial GHG emissions through audits and regulations for oil and gas fugitive emissions, gas transmission leaks, refinery methane, and flaring.
source_quote: Require assessment of large industrial sources to determine whether individual sources within a facility can cost-effectively reduce greenhouse gas emissions and provide other pollution reduction co-benefits. Reduce greenhouse gas emissions from fugitive emissions from oil and gas extraction and gas transmission. Adopt and implement regulations to control fugitive methane emissions and reduce flaring at refineries.
extraction_rationale: Umbrella industrial emissions policy with several regulatory submeasures.

parent_statement: Industrial Emissions
policy_statement: ARB will require major industrial facilities emitting over 0.5 MMTCO2E per year to conduct energy-efficiency and co-benefits audits.
source_quote: This measure would apply to the direct greenhouse gas emissions at major industrial facilities emitting more than 0.5 MMTCO2E per year. In general, these facilities also have significant emissions of criteria air pollutants, toxic air pollutants, or both. Major industrial facilities include power plants, refineries, cement plants, and miscellaneous other sources. ARB would implement this measure through a regulation, requiring each facility to conduct an energy efficiency audit of individual combustion and other direct sources of greenhouse gases within the facility to determine the potential reduction opportunities, including criteria air pollutants and toxic air contaminants.
section_header: ## Energy Efficiency and Co-Benefits Audits for Large Industrial Sources
extraction_rationale: Binding audit regulation with numeric threshold.

parent_statement: Industrial Emissions
policy_statement: ARB will develop oil and gas production and gas transmission measures to reduce methane leaks and incomplete combustion.
source_quote: Two measures would be developed to reduce methane emissions in the oil and gas production and gas transmission processes from leaks and incomplete combustion of methane (used as fuel). These measures would include improved leak detection, process modifications, equipment retrofits, installation of new equipment, and best management practices. The first measure would affect oil and gas producers.
section_header: ## Oil and Gas Recovery Operations and Transmission/Refineries
extraction_rationale: Specific methane regulations for oil and gas operations and transmission.

parent_statement: Industrial Emissions
policy_statement: ARB will limit refinery flare GHG emissions and remove the refinery fugitive methane exemption in most VOC regulations.
source_quote: Two measures would be developed for oil refineries. The first would limit the greenhouse gas emissions from refinery flares while preserving flaring as needed for safety reasons. The second would remove the current fugitive methane exemption in most refinery Volatile Organic Compounds (VOC) regulations.
section_header: ## Oil and Gas Recovery Operations and Transmission/Refineries
extraction_rationale: Specific refinery GHG regulatory changes.

policy_statement: California will support implementation of a high-speed rail system between northern and southern California.
source_quote: Support implementation of a high speed rail system. A high speed rail (HSR) system is part of the statewide strategy to provide more mobility choice and reduce greenhouse gas emissions. This measure supports implementation of plans to construct and operate a HSR system between northern and southern California.
extraction_rationale: Specific transportation infrastructure measure with GHG reduction purpose.

policy_statement: California will expand green building practices for new and existing buildings to reduce their carbon footprint.
source_quote: Expand the use of green building practices to reduce the carbon footprint of California's new and existing inventory of buildings. Collectively, energy use and related activities by buildings are the second largest contributor to California's greenhouse gas emissions. Almost one-quarter of California's greenhouse gas emissions can be attributed to buildings.
extraction_rationale: Umbrella green-building strategy with code, retrofit, performance, and public-building submeasures.

parent_statement: Green Building Strategy
policy_statement: California will move toward a mandatory Green Building Standards Code in 2011 and include zero-net-energy goals.
source_quote: In July 2008, the California Building Standards Commission (CBSC) adopted the Green Building Standards Code (GBSC) for all new construction in the state. While the current version of the commercial green building code is voluntary, CBSC anticipates adopting a mandatory code in 2011 which will institute minimum environmental performance standards for all occupancies. The Green Building Strategy includes Zero Net Energy (ZNE) goals for new and existing homes and commercial buildings consistent with the recently-adopted California Long Term Energy Efficiency Strategic Plan.
extraction_rationale: Specific building-code and zero-net-energy policy, though mandatory code is described as anticipated.

parent_statement: Green Building Strategy
policy_statement: California will establish building environmental performance rating systems and mechanisms to encourage or require retrofits for underperforming homes and commercial buildings.
source_quote: Furthermore, retrofitting existing residential and commercial buildings would achieve substantial greenhouse gas emissions reduction benefits. This Proposed Scoping Plan recommends the establishment of an environmental performance rating system for homes and commercial buildings and further recommends that California adopt mechanisms to encourage and require retrofits for buildings that do not meet minimum standards of performance. An effective green building framework can operate to deliver reductions of greenhouse gas emissions in multiple sectors.
extraction_rationale: Specific rating and retrofit mechanism for existing buildings.

parent_statement: Green Building Strategy
policy_statement: California will require new State buildings to meet LEED-NC Gold-like standards, retrofit existing State buildings to LEED-EB Silver-like standards, and require CHPS 2009 criteria for schools.
source_quote: Achieving significant greenhouse gas emissions reductions from new and existing buildings will require a combination of green building measures for new construction and retrofits to existing buildings. The State of California will set an example by requiring all new State buildings to exceed existing Green Building Initiative energy goals and achieve nationally-recognized building sustainability standards such as Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design - New Construction (LEED-NC) 'Gold' certification. Existing State buildings would also be retrofitted to achieve higher standards equivalent to LEED-EB for existing buildings (EB) 'Silver.'
extraction_rationale: Specific public building and school performance requirements; school funding condition is an edge case but concrete.

policy_statement: California will adopt direct regulations and mitigation fees to reduce high global warming potential gases.
source_quote: Adopt measures to reduce high global warming potential gases. High global warming potential (GWP) gases pose a unique challenge. Recommended measures to address this growing problem take the form of direct regulations and use of mitigation fees.
extraction_rationale: Umbrella policy for multiple high-GWP regulations and fees.

parent_statement: High Global Warming Potential Gases
policy_statement: ARB will implement discrete early actions for high-GWP gases in vehicle air conditioning, semiconductor manufacturing, air quality tracer studies, and consumer products.
source_quote: ARB identified four Discrete Early Action measures to reduce greenhouse gas emissions from the refrigerants used in car air conditioners, semiconductor manufacturing, air quality tracer studies, and consumer products. ARB has identified additional potential reduction opportunities based on specifications for future commercial and industrial refrigeration, changing the refrigerants used in auto air conditioning systems, and ensuring that existing car air conditioning systems as well as stationary refrigeration equipment do not leak. Recovery and destruction of high GWP materials in the banks described above could also provide significant reductions.
extraction_rationale: Specific early-action high-GWP controls; exact table rows include HFC-134a servicing, SF6 limits, PFCs, and consumer products.

parent_statement: High Global Warming Potential Gases
policy_statement: California will reduce high-GWP emissions from mobile and stationary sources through refrigerant substitution, leak testing, tracking, recovery, destruction, recycling, and alternative suppressants.
source_quote: ARB has identified additional potential reduction opportunities based on specifications for future commercial and industrial refrigeration, changing the refrigerants used in auto air conditioning systems, and ensuring that existing car air conditioning systems as well as stationary refrigeration equipment do not leak. Recovery and destruction of high GWP materials in the banks described above could also provide significant reductions. ARB is also proposing to establish an upstream mitigation fee on the use of high GWP gases.
section_header: ## Table 19:  High GWP Gases Sector Recommendation
extraction_rationale: Specific packages of mobile and stationary source high-GWP measures listed in Table 19.

parent_statement: High Global Warming Potential Gases
policy_statement: California will establish an upstream mitigation fee on high-GWP gases.
source_quote: ARB is also proposing to establish an upstream mitigation fee on the use of high GWP gases. Even with the reductions from the specific high GWP measures described above, this sector's emissions are still projected to more than double from current levels by 2020. An upstream fee would ensure that the climate impact of these substances is reflected in the total cost of the product, encouraging reduced use and end-of-life losses, as well as the development of alternatives.
extraction_rationale: Targeted fee intended to reduce high-GWP emissions and fund mitigation.

policy_statement: California will reduce landfill methane, increase waste diversion, composting, and commercial recycling, and move toward zero waste.
source_quote: Reduce methane emissions at landfills. Increase waste diversion, composting, and commercial recycling. Move toward zero-waste. California has a long track record of reducing greenhouse gas emissions by turning waste into resources, exemplified by the waste diversion rate from landfills of 54 percent (which exceeds the current 50 percent mandate) resulting from recovery of recyclable materials.
extraction_rationale: Umbrella waste-sector policy with methane and zero-waste submeasures.

parent_statement: Recycling and Waste
policy_statement: ARB and CIWMB will develop landfill methane control and pursue organics diversion and best practices at smaller landfills.
source_quote: Methane emissions from landfills, generated when wastes decompose, account for one percent of California's greenhouse gas emissions. Greenhouse gas emissions can be substantially reduced by properly managing all materials to minimize the generation of waste, maximize the diversion from landfills, and manage them to their highest and best use. Capturing landfill methane results in greenhouse gas benefits, as well as reductions in other air pollutants such as volatile organic compounds.
extraction_rationale: Specific landfill methane controls and waste-management actions.

parent_statement: Recycling and Waste
policy_statement: ARB and CIWMB will develop and implement high recycling and zero-waste programs, including commercial recycling, compost markets, anaerobic digestion, extended producer responsibility, and environmentally preferable purchasing.
source_quote: As noted by ETAAC, recycling in the commercial sector could be substantially increased. This could be implemented, for example, through voluntary or mandatory programs, including protocols, enhanced partnerships with local governments, and provision of appropriate financial incentives. ARB will work with CIWMB to develop and implement these types of programs.
extraction_rationale: Specific zero-waste program package; includes possible financial incentives.

policy_statement: California will preserve forest sequestration and encourage forest biomass for sustainable energy generation.
source_quote: Preserve forest sequestration and encourage the use of forest biomass for sustainable energy generation. The 2020 Proposed Scoping Plan target for California's forest sector is to maintain the current 5 MMTCO2E of sequestration through sustainable management practices, including reducing the risk of catastrophic wildfire, and the avoidance or mitigation of land-use changes that reduce carbon storage.
extraction_rationale: Umbrella nature-based carbon policy with a quantified sequestration target.

parent_statement: Sustainable Forests
policy_statement: California will maintain 5 MMTCO2E of forest-sector sequestration by 2020 through sustainable management, wildfire risk reduction, and avoidance or mitigation of land-use conversion.
source_quote: The 2020 Proposed Scoping Plan target for California's forest sector is to maintain the current 5 MMTCO2E of sequestration through sustainable management practices, including reducing the risk of catastrophic wildfire, and the avoidance or mitigation of land-use changes that reduce carbon storage. California's Board of Forestry and Fire Protection has the existing authority to provide for sustainable management practices, and will, at a minimum, work to maintain current carbon sequestration levels.
extraction_rationale: Quantified forest-carbon target delivered through ecosystem management.

parent_statement: Sustainable Forests
policy_statement: California will develop forest carbon monitoring and support public-funded voluntary conservation and sustainable forest-management projects with sequestration benefits.
source_quote: In addition, the Resources Agency is supporting voluntary actions, including expenditure of public funds for projects focused largely on conserving biodiversity, providing recreation, promoting sustainable forest management and other projects that also provide carbon sequestration benefits. The federal government must also use its regulatory authority to, at a minimum, maintain current carbon sequestration levels for land under its jurisdiction in California. Monitoring carbon sequestered on forest lands will be necessary to implement the target.
extraction_rationale: Combines public investment and monitoring mechanisms supporting the forest sequestration target.

policy_statement: California will continue water-efficiency programs and use cleaner energy sources to move and treat water.
source_quote: Continue efficiency programs and use cleaner energy sources to move and treat water. Water use requires significant amounts of energy. Approximately one-fifth of the electricity and one-third of the non-power plant natural gas consumed in the state are associated with water delivery, treatment and use.
extraction_rationale: Umbrella water-energy policy with six tabled submeasures.

parent_statement: Water
policy_statement: California will implement water use efficiency, water recycling, water-system energy efficiency, urban runoff reuse, and renewable energy production in the water sector.
source_quote: Six greenhouse gas emission reduction measures are proposed for the Water sector, and are shown in Table 21. Three of the measures target reducing energy requirements associated with providing reliable water supplies and two measures are aimed at reducing the amount of non-renewable electricity associated with conveying and treating water. The final measure focuses on providing sustainable funding for implementing these actions.
extraction_rationale: Groups W-1 through W-5 water-sector measures; primary mechanism is water and energy resource efficiency, except renewable energy as a mitigation component.

parent_statement: Water
policy_statement: California will pursue a public goods charge on water to fund water and energy efficiency, water recycling, and other GHG-reducing water management actions.
source_quote: ARB recommends a public goods charge for funding investments in water management actions that improve water and energy efficiency and reduce GHG emissions. As noted by the Economic and Technology Advancements Advisory Committee, a public goods charge on water can be collected on water bills and then used to fund end-use water efficiency improvements, system-wide efficiency projects, water recycling, and other actions that improve water and energy efficiency and reduce GHG emissions. Depending on how the fee schedule is developed in a subsequent rulemaking process, a public goods charge could generate $100 million to $500 million annually.
extraction_rationale: Specific fee mechanism with potential annual revenue and eligible uses.

policy_statement: California will encourage investment in manure digesters at large dairies and later determine whether the program should become mandatory by 2020.
source_quote: In the near-term, encourage investment in manure digesters and at the five-year Scoping Plan update determine if the program should be made mandatory by 2020. Encouraging the capture of methane through use of manure digester systems at dairies can provide emission reductions on a voluntary basis.
extraction_rationale: Agricultural methane policy with specific technology and potential mandatory transition.

parent_statement: Agriculture
policy_statement: California will use economic incentives such as marketable emission reduction credits, favorable utility contracts, and renewable energy incentives to support dairy manure digesters.
source_quote: Encouraging the capture of methane through use of manure digester systems at dairies can provide emission reductions on a voluntary basis. This measure is also a renewable energy strategy to promote the use of captured gas for fuels or power production. Initially, economic incentives such as marketable emission reduction credits, favorable utility contracts, or renewable energy incentives will be needed.
extraction_rationale: Specific financial incentive package for methane digester deployment.

parent_statement: Agriculture
policy_statement: ARB will reassess whether the voluntary manure digester approach should become mandatory for large dairies by 2020.
source_quote: ARB and the California Climate Action Registry worked together on a manure digester protocol to establish methods for quantifying greenhouse gas emissions reductions from individual projects; the Board adopted this protocol in September 2008. The voluntary approach will be re-assessed at the five-year update of the Scoping Plan to determine if the program should become mandatory for large dairies by 2020.
extraction_rationale: Concrete review point with potential mandatory regulatory outcome.

policy_statement: ARB will research nitrogen fertilizer N2O emissions and explore agricultural reduction opportunities.
source_quote: Nitrogen fertilizer, which produces N2O emissions, is the other significant source of greenhouse gases in the Agricultural sector. ARB has begun a research program to better understand the variables affecting fertilizer N2O emissions (Phase 1), and based on the findings, will explore opportunities for emission reductions (Phase 2). There may be significant potential for additional voluntary reductions in the agricultural sector through strategies, such as those recommended by ETAAC.
extraction_rationale: Specific research-to-policy pathway for agricultural emissions; additional strategies are partly exploratory.

policy_statement: California will explore additional voluntary agricultural reductions from equipment fuel efficiency, water use efficiency, biomass utilization, and carbon sequestration on rangelands and reforested woodlands.
source_quote: There may be significant potential for additional voluntary reductions in the agricultural sector through strategies, such as those recommended by ETAAC. These opportunities include increases in fuel efficiency of on-farm equipment, water use efficiency, and biomass utilization for fuels and power production. Increasing carbon sequestration, including on working rangelands, hardwood and riparian woodland reforestation, also hold potential as a greenhouse gas strategies.
extraction_rationale: Exploratory voluntary agricultural actions, but specific interventions are named.

policy_statement: ARB will recognize and reward voluntary early GHG reductions before full AB 32 implementation.
source_quote: ARB is required to design regulations to encourage early action to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, and to provide appropriate recognition or credit for that action. Recognizing and rewarding greenhouse gas emissions reductions that occur prior to the full implementation of the AB 32 program can set the stage for innovation by incentivizing the development and employment of new clean technologies and by generating economic and environmental benefits for California.
extraction_rationale: Named voluntary early-action crediting policy with allowance submechanisms.

parent_statement: Voluntary Early Action
policy_statement: ARB will review voluntary GHG reduction quantification methodologies and issue Executive Orders confirming technical soundness where appropriate.
source_quote: In February 2008, ARB adopted a policy statement encouraging the early reductions of greenhouse gas emissions. The policy statement describes a process for interested parties to submit proposed emission quantification methodologies for voluntary greenhouse gas emissions reductions to ARB for review. The intent is to provide a rapid assessment of methodologies for evaluating potential greenhouse gas emissions reduction projects to encourage early actions.
extraction_rationale: Concrete administrative mechanism for voluntary early reductions.

parent_statement: Voluntary Early Action
policy_statement: ARB will provide credit for qualified voluntary early reductions through allowance set-asides, allocation rules, and early-action recognition in other regulations.
source_quote: ARB will provide appropriate credit for voluntary early reductions that can be adequately quantified and verified through three primary means. First, within the cap-and-trade program, ARB would set aside a certain number of allowances from the first compliance period to use to reward voluntary reductions that occur before 2012. In addition, ARB will assure that the allocation process in the first compliance period does not disadvantage facilities that have made reductions after AB 32 went into effect at the start of 2007 and before 2012.
extraction_rationale: Concrete allowance and regulatory crediting mechanism.

policy_statement: ARB will adopt methodologies for quantifying voluntary reductions and potentially allow verified offsets from unregulated emissions-reduction projects.
source_quote: Emissions reduction projects that are not otherwise regulated, covered under an emissions cap, or undertaken as a result of government incentive programs can generate 'offsets.' These are verifiable reductions whose ownership can be transferred to others. Voluntary offset markets have recently flourished as a way for companies and individuals to offset their own emissions by purchasing reductions outside of their own operations.
extraction_rationale: Umbrella voluntary reductions and offsets policy.

parent_statement: Voluntary Reductions
policy_statement: ARB will adopt quantification methodologies for voluntary reductions, including forest projects, local government operations, urban forestry, and manure digesters.
source_quote: ARB will adopt methodologies for quantifying voluntary reductions. (HSC §38571) The Board adopted a methodology for forest projects in October 2007, and for local government operations, urban forestry, and manure digesters in September 2008. The recognition of voluntary reduction or offset methodologies does not in any way guarantee that these offsets can be used for other compliance purposes.
extraction_rationale: Concrete methodology adoption policy; nature-based examples are explicitly included.

policy_statement: ARB will evaluate use of allowance auction revenues and targeted fees to support GHG reductions and AB 32 socio-economic goals.
source_quote: Revenues may be generated from the implementation of various proposed components of the Scoping Plan, including by the use of auctions within a cap-and-trade system or through the imposition of more targeted measures, such as a public goods charge on water. These revenues could be used to support AB 32 requirements for greenhouse gas emissions reductions and associated socio-economic considerations. This section summarizes some of the recommendations and ideas that ARB has received to date.
section_header: ## E. Use of Allowances and Revenues
extraction_rationale: Broad revenue-use framework tied to carbon-pricing and targeted fees.

policy_statement: California may create a California Carbon Trust to use allowance or carbon-fee revenues, leveraged with private funds, to support climate program goals.
source_quote: The Economic and Technology Advancement Advisory Committee (ETAAC) recommended the creation of a California Carbon Trust as a possible mechanism for using revenues generated by the program, leveraged with private funds, to further the overall program goals. ETAAC's recommendation is roughly based on the United Kingdom Carbon Trust. The United Kingdom program was established with public funds, but now functions as a standalone corporation, providing management and consulting services to corporations and small and medium businesses on reducing greenhouse gas emissions.
section_header: ## E. Use of Allowances and Revenues
extraction_rationale: Specific proposed climate finance institution; recommendation rather than adopted final commitment.

policy_statement: California may use program revenues to fund climate adaptation programs, and the Resources Agency will prepare a State Climate Adaptation Strategy by early 2009.
source_quote: - Climate change adaptation programs Climate change will impact natural and human environments. Program revenues could be used to help the state adapt to the effects of climate change which will be detailed in the State's Climate Adaptation Strategy being prepared by the Resources Agency to be completed in early 2009.
section_header: ## E. Use of Allowances and Revenues
extraction_rationale: Potential adaptation funding use and a named adaptation planning commitment with date.

policy_statement: California will launch a robust statewide climate public outreach and education program coordinated by a Climate Action Team steering team.
source_quote: To be successful, a climate action program needs an effective public outreach and education program. The Proposed Plan calls for a robust statewide program designed to generate awareness and involvement in California's climate change efforts. The Climate Action Team will convene a steering team that includes State agencies and other public agencies such as the state's air districts, and public and private utilities, which have a strong track record of successful efforts at public education to reduce driving (Spare the Air) or promote energy efficiency and reduce energy demand.
extraction_rationale: Specific statewide outreach program and coordinating body; primarily supports climate implementation rather than directly reducing emissions.

policy_statement: By 2010, California will develop climate change education components for the State's new K-12 model school curriculum.
source_quote: Setting California on track to a low-carbon future beyond 2020 will be a multigenerational challenge. To meet this challenge, climate-related education in schools must be a central element of California's plan. By 2010, California will develop climate change education components to the State's new K-12 model school curriculum as part of the Education and the Environment Initiative (AB 1548, Pavley, Chapter 665, Statutes of 2003).
extraction_rationale: Specific education policy with a 2010 deadline; climate relevance is direct but emissions impact is enabling/indirect.

policy_statement: California will strengthen green workforce development through career technical education, skilled-worker pipelines, and higher education clean-tech training.
source_quote: The following strategies will be key to ensure that California's workforce is equipped to help lead the transition to a clean energy future: - Strengthen and expand access to Career and Technical Education (CTE) in California public schools for the next generation of workers who will build a green economy. - Ensure an adequate pipeline of skilled workers who are trained in the new technologies of a greener economy.
extraction_rationale: Specific workforce-development strategies for clean energy implementation. It is an enabling policy with climate relevance through mitigation workforce capacity.

policy_statement: ARB and State partners will develop an online small business toolkit for AB 32 implementation, including carbon footprint tools, GHG inventory protocol, best practices, financing resources, and an awards program.
source_quote: One of ARB's Early Action measures is designed to help businesses during AB 32 implementation. With our State partners, we are developing an on-line small business 'toolkit' designed for small and medium-sized businesses that will provide a one-stop shop for technical and financial resources. Toolkit components will include a business-specific calculator to assess a company's carbon footprint; a voluntary greenhouse gas inventory protocol for measuring greenhouse gas emissions; recommended best practices for energy, transportation, building, purchasing, and recycling; case studies demonstrating how small and medium California businesses have reduced greenhouse gas emissions; program financing resources; peernetworking opportunities; and an awards program to recognize reductions of greenhouse gas emissions among California businesses.
extraction_rationale: Specific named assistance toolkit with technical and financial resources; enabling policy for small-business GHG reductions.

policy_statement: ARB and other State agencies will develop Scoping Plan regulations and programs through rulemaking and stakeholder engagement.
source_quote: This Proposed Scoping Plan outlines the regulations and other mechanisms needed to reduce greenhouse gas emissions in California. ARB and other State agencies will work closely with stakeholders and the public to develop regulatory measures and other programs to implement the Plan. ARB and other State agencies will develop any regulations in accordance with established rulemaking guidelines.
extraction_rationale: Implementation commitment for the plan's climate regulations and programs.

policy_statement: ARB will update the Scoping Plan at least every five years.
source_quote: ARB will update the plan at least once every five years (HSC §38561(h)). These updates will allow ARB to evaluate the progress made toward the State's greenhouse gas emission reduction goals and correct the Plan's course where necessary. This section discusses the tracking and measurement of progress that ARB envisions.
extraction_rationale: Statutory climate planning update requirement.

policy_statement: Every State agency must prepare an annual GHG Report Card, and agencies must obtain outside GHG audits every three years as funds are available.
source_quote: SB 85 (Budget Committee, Chapter 178, Statutes of 2007) requires every State agency to prepare an annual 'Report Card,' detailing measures the agency has adopted and taken to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, including the actual emissions reduced as a result of those actions. The information must be submitted to CalEPA, which is then required to compile all the State agency data into a report format, which is made available on the Internet and submitted to the Legislature. Agencies are also required, as funds are available, to have an outside audit of greenhouse gas-related actions completed every three years to verify actual and projected reductions.
extraction_rationale: Binding reporting and audit requirements for state agencies.

policy_statement: ARB will require annual mandatory GHG emissions reporting from the largest California facilities, with third-party verification beginning in 2010.
source_quote: ARB's mandatory reporting rule, adopted in December 2007, will help the State obtain facility-level data from the largest sources of greenhouse gas emissions in California. The regulation requires annual reporting from the largest facilities in the state, accounting for 94 percent of greenhouse gas emissions from industrial and commercial stationary sources in California. Beginning in 2010, emissions reports will be more rigorous and will be subject to third-party verification.
extraction_rationale: Binding emissions reporting regulation with coverage and verification requirements.

policy_statement: ARB and partner agencies will enforce Scoping Plan regulations to ensure planned GHG reductions are achieved.
source_quote: Enforcement is a critical component of all of the State's regulatory programs, both to ensure that emissions are actually reduced and to provide a level playing field for entities complying with the law. To meet the 2020 target this plan calls for aggressive action by a number of State agencies. Each of those agencies will employ its full range of compliance and enforcement options to ensure that planned reductions are achieved.
extraction_rationale: Concrete enforcement commitment for plan regulations.

policy_statement: ARB will develop a comprehensive cap-and-trade enforcement plan, administer penalties for insufficient allowances or reporting failures, and formalize WCI enforcement agreements.
source_quote: Although many of the measures in the Proposed Scoping Plan are modeled on existing ARB regulations, a multi-sector, regional cap-and-trade program would bring unique enforcement challenges. ARB and CalEPA have begun the process of engaging and consulting with other State agencies, such as California's Department of Justice, Public Utilities Commission, Energy Commission, as well as the Independent System Operator, on market tracking and enforcement. These working group meetings are ongoing and will culminate in a comprehensive enforcement plan to accompany the proposed cap-and-trade program when the Board considers regulatory requirements.
extraction_rationale: Specific enforcement architecture for cap-and-trade. It governs a financial instrument but is itself an enforcement policy, not a separate financial instrument.

policy_statement: ARB will initiate a fee-program rulemaking to fund AB 32 administration, implementation, and enforcement.
source_quote: Administration, implementation, and enforcement of the emissions reduction measures contained in the Proposed Scoping Plan will require a stable and continuing source of funding. AB 32 authorizes ARB to collect fees to fund implementation of the statute. This fall ARB will initiate a rulemaking for a fee program to fund administration of the program.
extraction_rationale: Specific fee program for climate program funding.

policy_statement: California will participate in the International Carbon Action Partnership while designing its mandatory carbon market program.
source_quote: California is also a charter member of the International Carbon Action Partnership (ICAP), an organization composed of countries and regions that have adopted carbon caps and that are actively pursuing the implementation of carbon markets through mandatory cap-and-trade systems. California's continued involvement in ICAP will be very beneficial for sharing experiences and knowledge as we design our own market program.
extraction_rationale: Named international carbon-market partnership supporting the State's carbon pricing program.

policy_statement: California will consider state-provincial partnerships with developing jurisdictions that pledge GHG intensity targets or sector benchmarks.
source_quote: California can advance the international policy debate through state-provincial partnerships for achieving early climate action in developing countries. This approach envisions commitments by developed countries to provide capacity building through technological assistance and investment support in return for developing countries adopting enhanced mitigation actions. California will consider working with developing countries or provinces that have, at a minimum, pledged to achieve greenhouse gas intensity targets in certain carbon-intensive sectors through mechanisms, such as minimum performance standards or sector benchmarks.
extraction_rationale: Specific international partnership model; framed as under consideration.

policy_statement: California will support forest carbon activities in developing countries, including REDD-like conservation, restoration, reforestation, and sustainable financing mechanisms.
source_quote: California also hopes to engage developing countries, including Brazil and Indonesia, to reduce emissions and sequester carbon through eligible forest carbon activities. Activities aimed at Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation (REDD) were excluded from the rules governing the first Kyoto commitment period, but there is considerable momentum behind the effort to include provisions that would recognize such activities in a post2012 international agreement. Providing incentives to developing countries to help cut emissions by preserving standing forests, and to sequester additional carbon through the restoration and reforestation of degraded lands and forests and improved forest management practices, will be crucial in bringing those countries into the global climate protection effort.
extraction_rationale: Nature-based international mitigation policy with incentive and financing mechanisms; somewhat aspirational.

policy_statement: California should support near-term advancement of carbon capture and storage and establish a framework to credit CCS projects when appropriate.
source_quote: According to a 2005 report by the Intergovernmental Panel for Climate Change (IPCC), a power plant with CCS could reduce CO2 emissions to the atmosphere by approximately 80 to 90 percent compared to a plant without CCS (including the energy used to capture, compress and transport CO2). While more research and development needs to occur, California should both support near-term advancement of the technology and ensure that an adequate framework is in place to provide credit for CCS projects when appropriate.
extraction_rationale: Specific CCS technology advancement and crediting framework; phrased as 'should' and dependent on further R&D.

policy_statement: California will use a 2030 trajectory benchmark of reducing statewide GHG emissions below 300 MMTCO2E to stay on course toward the 2050 target.
source_quote: To stay on course toward the 2050 target our State's greenhouse gas emissions need to be reduced to below 300 MMTCO2E by 2030. This translates to an average reduction of four percent per year between 2020 and 2030. An additional challenge comes from the fact that California's population is expected to grow by about 12 percent between 2020 and 2030.
section_header: ## C. Reducing California's Emissions Further A Look Forward to 2030
extraction_rationale: Quantified 2030 trajectory benchmark; surrounding text notes the future policy mix is illustrative, so this is less binding than the 2020 and 2050 targets.

policy_statement: Reduce Chicago's greenhouse gas emissions by at least 62% by 2040.
source_quote: The 2022 CAP aims to chart an equitable path to reduce Chicago's GHG emissions by a minimum of 62% by 2040. Following the principles defined in this plan, this pathway prioritizes improving the lives of all Chicagoans by promoting environmental justice, generating household savings, improving community health, transitioning away from fossil-fuel dependency, and ensuring that all Chicago communities are prepared for the undeniable impacts of climate change, by 2040.
extraction_rationale: Quantified plan-wide GHG reduction target with a deadline; the quote also explicitly names preparedness for climate impacts.

policy_statement: Allocate $188 million through the Chicago Recovery Plan for climate resiliency and mitigation.
source_quote: In October 2021, Chicago's City Council approved $188 million for climate resiliency and mitigation, as part of Mayor Lori Lightfoot's $2.5 billion Chicago Recovery Plan. This historic level of investment toward climate action will provide funding for resilient infrastructure and green workforce development opportunities.
extraction_rationale: City Council-approved public investment line for climate resiliency and mitigation; qualifies as a financial instrument.

source_quote:

extraction_rationale: Specific allocated budget line with named deliverables; qualifies as a financial instrument.

source_quote:

section_header: Chicago Recovery Plan funding overlap with Chicago's 2022 Climate Action Plan
extraction_rationale: Specific allocated budget line with named deliverables; qualifies as a financial instrument.

source_quote:

The project will decrease the energy burden on organizations and provide critical services to underserved communities.Thisprogramaimstodevelopanetworkofresiliencyhubsthroughout Chicagoandprovideenergyeducationservicesandshelterduringextremeweather.
section_header: Chicago Recovery Plan funding overlap with Chicago's 2022 Climate Action Plan
extraction_rationale: Specific allocated budget line with named deliverables; qualifies as a financial instrument.

policy_statement: Allocate $5 million to enable retrofits and install solar panels at up to 10 Chicago Public Libraries.
source_quote:
## Chicago Recovery Plan funding overlap with Chicago's 2022 Climate Action Plan

Library Power Project                               | $5 million         | Enable retrofits and install solar panels at up to 10 Chicago Public Libraries, mini - mizingutilitycostsandensuringthatwesustainourlibraryassetsforthelongterm.
section_header: Chicago Recovery Plan funding overlap with Chicago's 2022 Climate Action Plan
extraction_rationale: Specific allocated budget line with named deliverables; qualifies as a financial instrument.

policy_statement: Allocate $5 million to generate community solar energy on industrial roofs for at least hundreds of households.

extraction_rationale: Specific industrial and oil-and-gas energy efficiency actions.

parent_statement: Maximizing energy efficiency
policy_statement: Improve efficiency of appliances, equipment, transport, buildings, and facilities, and implement the National Green Building Code.
